title: Who comes first on the ballot?
hook: Would an identical candidate gain from moving to the first row?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Separate presentation order from candidate attributes and note the low-information context.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Separate presentation order from candidate attributes and note the low-information context.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy ballot lists A, B, C. A randomized reorder lists B, C, A. What position does A occupy after reordering? Toy inputs A=[3, 1, 2]; B=[1, 2, 3].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[3, 1, 2], [1, 2, 3]]. Labels: A position, B position, C position.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Presentation order can be changed while candidate identities remain fixed. The two arrangements make that manipulation observable. A change in vote share would be a separate outcome, and cannot be calculated from position alone.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses A position=1, B position=2, C position=3. What is A position? Answer: 1.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses A position=1, B position=2, C position=3. What is A position?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 1. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Candidates listed first on ballots gain votes, especially in low-information races (Koppell & Steen, 2004).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Separate presentation order from candidate attributes and note the low-information context.
